title: Integral Brown hypotheses are equivalent to uniform constructible Ext bounds
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite intermediate field in the fixed algebraic closure, and $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring]. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\ne\ell$, and let $X$ be separated and finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Use constructible sheaves with finite constant models [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Then the Brown bundle [lem-sfb-brown-hypotheses-criterion] holds for $\Lambda,X$ if and only if for every constructible sheaf $C$ there exists an integer $d_C$ such that, for every constructible sheaf $N$ and integer $q>d_C$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})}(C[0],N[0][q])$ is zero. This is the ambient Ext group [def-pc-ext]. The bound may depend on C but is uniform over N. No finiteness of the cohomological dimension of k is assumed; the equivalence does not assert either side unconditionally.

proof.text: For integral coefficients, finite constant local models have Tor interval [-1,0]. Stratified Tor descent gives the same interval for every constructible sheaf. The cohomology-interval lemma gives Tor interval [a-1,b] for a bounded constructible complex with cohomology in [a,b]. Choose a lower bound min(a,b) so the interval is nonempty even for zero objects. Thus Dctf=Dbc, and applying localizingClosure to this equality gives equality of their localizing closures. This proves only the needed integral comparison, without using the broad comparison theorem or its finite-ring examples. Finite type over the field makes X compact and locally Noetherian, so the admissible Noetherian Brown criterion applies.

Assume the Brown bundle. A constructible sheaf in degree zero is bounded constructible: its degree-zero homology is itself, its other homology objects are zero. Repleteness and existence of a constructible zero object give constructibility in every degree. By the integral Tor equality this single object is in Dctf and hence in its localizing closure. Apply the Brown uniform-heart Ext bound to this compact source. Every constructible second sheaf also belongs to the closure, so this gives the required bound over all such sheaves. Converting positive integer degrees to naturals identifies the asserted Hom groups exactly.

Choose a nonnegative natural bound for each constructible sheaf using Int.toNat and weaken each degree inequality by Int.self_le_toNat. Apply integralConstructibleCompactness with these explicit bounds. Its compactness clause gives coproducts and compactness of all bounded constructible objects in Loc(Dbc). Rewrite this entire witness along the already established equality Loc(Dctf)=Loc(Dbc), then restrict its compactness clause to the bounded-constructible part of each Dctf object. The Noetherian Brown criterion assembles the bundle. No second coproduct witness or objectwise transport theorem is required, and no Ext bound is inferred from positive characteristic.

theorem brownHypothesesFor_padicIntegers_iff_ext_bounded
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] :
    BrownHypothesesFor (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X ↔
      ∀ C : ConstantModelConstructible (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X,
        ∃ d : ℤ,
          ∀ N : ConstantModelConstructible (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X,
            ∀ q : ℤ, d < q →
              Subsingleton (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj C.obj) ⟶
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N.obj)⟦q⟧)
